_source: CLAUDE.md §42 EXPERIMENT INFRASTRUCTURE & LIFECYCLE. The ten lifecycle stages and the twenty-two required fields below are §42's own lists, in §42's order and wording. scripts/tests/test_experiment.py parses them back out of CLAUDE.md, so a twenty-third field in the spec fails the build rather than going unrecorded.
_reader: scripts/experiment.py is the ONE writer and the ONE reader of the experiment store. Records live under docs/experiments/ as one JSON file per experiment, append-only.
_immutable: CLAUDE.md §42: 'Experiment records must be immutable.' Enforced three ways, because a convention is not an enforcement: a sealed record is a MappingProxyType whose mutation raises; writing to a path that already exists raises rather than overwriting; and re-sealing a record whose content hash does not match its stored hash raises. The point is not that nobody would edit one -- it is that an edited one must be DETECTABLE, because an experiment record is the only evidence that a candidate earned its way into production (§41, §47).
_relationship_to_41: §41's pipeline (11 stages, trading outcomes -> human decision) is the LEARNING loop; §42's lifecycle (10 stages, observation -> approval/rejection) is the EXPERIMENT record of one trip around it. They are different lists in the spec and are declared separately; `stage_of_41` maps each §42 stage onto the §41 stage it corresponds to, so the two cannot drift into describing different processes.

fields.definition: Stable id of this experiment, unique in the store. Derived from the timestamp and a slug of the hypothesis so two experiments cannot silently share one.
The version of the system this candidate is a change TO (§47). Without it a result cannot be attributed to anything.
The version this candidate would become if approved (§47's v1 -> candidate v1.x -> approved v2).
What is believed to be true and what would falsify it. §45: 'Actively attempt to disprove candidates.'
Why this experiment was run at all. Distinct from the hypothesis: the motivation is the cost being paid, and §43's experiment budget counts it.
The §41 cluster this candidate answers, or an explicit statement that it answers none -- a candidate with no failure behind it is a parameter search, and §43 needs to be able to tell them apart.
§10's record of the data this run read. scripts/snapshot.py dataset_snapshot().
§11's record of the configuration behind the result, captured BY VALUE. scripts/snapshot.py config_snapshot().
The §33 account profile in force, by value -- a result measured on a 15 % drawdown account is not the same result on a 5 % one.
§34's risk numbers by value: the per-trade ceiling, the R:R floor, the fee and slippage model.
§24-§32's event-risk settings: buffers, impact policy, the fail-safe action, and the calendar snapshot id.
§21's session model as it applied: which sessions, which timezone rules, which killzones.
Every parameter the candidate changes AND the values they had. A diff, not a dump: 'what was different' is the experiment.
The seed of every stochastic step (bootstrap, Monte Carlo, resampling). §46: a result without it is not reproducible. `null` is allowed only with an explicit statement that nothing stochastic ran.
The in-sample, out-of-sample and holdout ranges, named separately. §44 needs to know which period was exposed.
§45's method: in-sample, OOS, walk-forward, sensitivity, regime, Monte Carlo, perturbation, stress.
§39's twenty-three, from scripts/performance.py, WITH sample size. Not a chosen subset: a subset is a selection, and selections are what §43 counts.
§45's sensitivity and perturbation output, or an explicit unavailable() with the reason.
APPROVED / REJECTED / DEFERRED, and who decided. §41 reserves this for a human.
When the experiment was recorded, UTC.
The git commit the run executed at, plus whether the tree was dirty. §46: a dirty tree means the commit does not identify the code.
The Trading System registry version this experiment ran against (§35/§47).

_pending: PENDING is not one of §42's own words -- §42 lists `decision` as a field and §41 names the three outcomes. PENDING is the honest value of that field BEFORE the human has decided, and it exists so that a record can be sealed at the moment the evidence is complete rather than waiting for a decision that may take days. A PENDING record is immutable like any other; the decision is recorded by sealing a SUCCESSOR record that names its predecessor, never by editing one.
